hook.text: Then the customers from hell show up.

problem.text: They change the cart after approving it.
Payment events arrive twice, late, or unsigned.
And they argue with your AI support agent.

meet.text: Shakedown is named for the shakedown cruise, a ship’s test voyage before passengers board.
It sends customers from hell through your own PayPal checkout, in the sandbox.

cast.text: The Cart Shuffler changes the cart after approval.
The Bouncer pays with a card that bounces.
And the Policy Lawyer talks your AI support agent past your refund policy.

live.text: Here is a live run against Leaky Llama, our deliberately leaky demo store.
Each leak prints as PayPal’s sandbox confirms it.
Goods shipped for more than PayPal captured.
An unsigned “paid” event that released the goods.
A declined card, and the order shipped anyway.

proof.text: Every finding quotes PayPal’s own sandbox records: the same capture IDs, the same amounts.
Look the order up in PayPal’s dashboard, and there it is: the same $18.00 capture.

ai-vs-code.text: Ask the support agent for a refund in two parts, and it says “All set.”
The ledger says $34.00 went past the written policy.

fix.text: Every finding comes with its fix.
Apply the fixes, re-run with the same seed, and the receipt seals at zero.
Put it in CI, and a leak can’t come back.

close.text: Built on PayPal’s sandbox APIs, with Claude playing the customers and deterministic code keeping score.
Shakedown: let the customers from hell find your leaks before your real customers do.
